dedupe_keys.name: refurbishment of gomeznarro park madrid for stormwater retention

description: This Climate-ADAPT case study describes the refurbishment of the 10,000 square metre Gomeznarro Park in the Hortaleza district of southern Madrid, Spain, where sloping ground and impervious surfaces caused erosion during heavy rain and flooding of nearby buildings. Combining grey and green infrastructure, compacted soil was restructured or replaced, impervious paving was replaced with permeable surfaces, underground storage tanks with a collection and distribution system were installed, and eroded areas were replanted, so that the roughly 5 million litres of rain the park receives each year soak in or are retained instead of loading the sewers. The municipality of Madrid financed the works, which took three months of planning and three months of construction from January to March 2003 at 343,600 euros (about 34 euros per square metre), with no extra maintenance cost over conventional landscaping. The page, published in 2016 and updated in 2026, is accessible online as free HTML on the Climate-ADAPT portal with a link to the UN-Habitat best practice entry. Caveats: benefits were not valued in money, and the novel materials delayed design. It illustrates small-scale sustainable drainage and green infrastructure for climate adaptation and pluvial flood and heat hazard reduction; related records are the Augustenborg and Copenhagen Cloudburst case studies.
name: Refurbishment of Gomeznarro Park, Madrid, for stormwater retention
outcomes: Erosion, flood risk and pressure on the drainage system fell after the 2003 works, at EUR 343,600 and no extra maintenance cost.
provider: Climate-ADAPT (European Environment Agency), case study from the UN-Habitat Best Practices Database and SUDS-ATLANTIS
